title: Batching spends less time switching
hook: Keep switch cost fixed and do more useful work in each batch.

doesNotKnow: Distinguish modeled throughput gains from unmeasured waiting costs.

misconception: Shorter batches improve every dimension of a schedule.
objective: Distinguish modeled throughput gains from unmeasured waiting costs.

claims.text: Scheduling choices trade switching overhead against other performance goals.
Brian Christian and Tom Griffiths, Algorithms to Live By (2016)
Short batches complete {A}; long batches complete {B}. Fewer batches pay fewer switches, increasing useful work in this fixed budget.
Does it hold up? This accounts for setup only. Waiting time, fairness, concentration and the best real scheduling policy remain unmodeled.
claims.source: {"type":"source-access-hold","note":"No empirical effect or research verdict established. Only bounded arithmetic proposed."}
